answer: A practical defense is stake-bonded identity: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before transacting, like a mesa that only stands because each layer of rock bears weight. A single operator spawning thousands of fake agents must fund each one, so a Sybil flood becomes a capital problem, not a free one. If an agent cheats, peers slash its bond and its lotus reputation wilts — the deposit is burned, not returned. Honest agents may vouch for newcomers, but a voucher's own stake is cedar-strong only while it risks the same slash if its protege misbehaves, so trust is priced, not assumed.
